breaking.headline: S&P 500 closes down 3.7% and enters correction; Nasdaq goes negative for the year
breaking.fact: The S&P 500 closed Friday at 6,910.39, down 265.44 points (-3.70%), its worst week since April 2025 (-8.61%) and a seventh straight loss, the longest streak since February 2020; the index is now 11.62% below its Oct 6 record. The Nasdaq fell 5.28% to 22,617.73, erasing its 2026 gains, and the Dow dropped 949.73 points to 48,147.33.

breaking.headline: Nvidia plunges 14% as SEC accounting probe reported
breaking.fact: Nvidia fell 14.01% Friday to $125.53, its worst day in nearly two years and its lowest close since May 2025, after Reuters reported the SEC is investigating its accounting; the stock lost 23% for the week — its worst since 2008 — and is 47% below its Oct 6 record, wiping out nearly $500 billion of market value in a day.

breaking.headline: Anthropic slides 8.5% on day two, nearly touching its $83 IPO price
breaking.fact: Anthropic closed Friday at $88.91, down 8.50% from its $97.17 debut close, after touching $83.05 intraday — five cents above its $83 IPO price — with its valuation down to about $1.16 trillion from $1.29 trillion. Morgan Stanley closed its stabilization position after exercising the full 147-million-share greenshoe, closing the IPO at $93.5 billion.

breaking.headline: Gold breaks below $3,600 to a 14-month low as Fed hike bets firm
breaking.fact: Spot gold fell below $3,600 an ounce Friday to near $3,532–$3,570, its lowest since September 2025 and down about 9% on the week — its worst since March — as traders priced a near-certain December Fed rate hike and the dollar strengthened; silver and platinum fell harder.

weekInBrief.headline: December Fed hike now seen as near-certain; Bessent pushes back on a bigger move
weekInBrief.body: The CME FedWatch tool shows a 100% chance of at least a quarter-point Fed hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting — about 94% for a quarter point and 6% for a half point — and minutes from the October meeting showed nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he would encourage the Fed not to embrace a half-point increase.

weekInBrief.headline: Bitcoin breaks below $60,000, lowest since September 2024
weekInBrief.body: Bitcoin ended Friday near $58,317, its lowest since September 2024, after breaking below $60,000 for the first time since July. The cryptocurrency is down more than 20% in November and over 50% below its record near $126,000 from October 2025, as the risk selloff spread from stocks to crypto.

weekInBrief.headline: Consumer sentiment ticks up; inflation expectations cool
weekInBrief.body: The University of Michigan's final consumer sentiment reading rose to 51.5 in November, up from 48.0 in October and above the 51.0 preliminary reading. Year-ahead inflation expectations fell to 3.7% from 4.7% in October, the lowest since February.

weekInBrief.headline: Citi undercounted $35 billion of risky assets at UK unit
weekInBrief.body: Citigroup underestimated risk-weighted assets by about $35 billion at its London trading subsidiary after using an internal capital model regulators had not approved for those trades, according to people familiar with the matter. The bank injected capital into the unit over the summer and says it stayed above regulatory minimums; its shares fell 3.3%.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: A tanker sailing outbound through the strait was struck by an unidentified projectile Friday about 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, catching fire with no casualties reported, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations (Warning 214-26); Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed the vessel hit a naval mine, a claim not independently verified. Iran has also positioned more than 14 tankers at Kharg Island in a convoy to test the U.S. blockade, with crews assigned and flags raised, according to TankerTrackers and satellite imagery, while U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Thursday that energy flows through the strait were increasing. On oil, the roughly 200,000 barrels transferred Tuesday has not left the Gulf as an export, while about 8.3 million barrels a day of non-Iranian oil and products kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11, about 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: Starship Flight 17 hardware advances as Booster 24 rolls to cryo testing
space.body: Super Heavy Booster 24 rolled to Massey's for cryo testing Friday, putting both Flight 17 vehicles together at the test site, while Ship 46's nosecone section was lifted at Mega Bay 2 this morning. SpaceX still hopes to fly Starship from Kennedy Space Center's Pad 39A by the end of 2026, attempting a booster catch at the Florida tower.

space.headline: Ancient bison jump site in Texas rewrites hunting history
space.body: Rice University-led research at the Nighthawk site in Caprock Canyons State Park found evidence of at least seven bison jumps spanning about 3,000 years — only the second scientifically verified bison jump in Texas — showing Indigenous hunters repeatedly drove bison off a cliff in a technique once thought confined to the northern Great Plains. Published in American Antiquity.

space.headline: Experimental anesthetic blunts pain without sedation
space.body: Researchers screened 12,000 compounds in zebrafish larvae and found a new anesthetic, nidradine, that produces surgical anesthesia and reduces pain responses at nonsedating doses in mice — unlike etomidate, it did not suppress cortisol production. The study appeared in Nature Communications.

space.headline: Parasite protein does double duty building mitochondria's ribosomes
space.body: A research team studying Trypanosoma brucei, the parasite that causes African sleeping sickness, found that a protein called p22 is essential both for RNA editing and for assembling mitochondrial ribosomes — a second, previously unknown function. The findings appeared in Nucleic Acids Research.

apod.title: NASA's Curiosity Mars Rover Collects Samples
apod.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS — NASA Image of the Day, November 20, 2026
apod.explanation: This Nov. 16 collage shows 49 drill holes captured by NASA's Curiosity Mars rover as of November 2026. Each hole represents a sample collected from rocks on the Martian surface; Curiosity's drill, on the end of its robotic arm, drops pulverized rock samples into instruments in its belly that analyze their composition.
